name: Marrow Broadcast
description:
Marrow Broadcast is defined by a single radical technical premise: all compositions must be designed for transmission through bone-conduction systems and subdermal speaker implants, never through conventional audio channels. The result is a genre that exists in a fundamentally private register — felt as much as heard, vibrating through the skull and chest cavity, perceived as simultaneously internal and external. Composers engineer their work to exploit the specific resonant properties of bone and tissue, creating harmonic content that interacts with the listener's own body as an instrument, producing different experiences for listeners of different physiologies.

The genre emerged in the 2190s from lower-tier communities where conventional audio equipment was unaffordable or confiscated, but subdermal implants — originally medical devices — were common enough to be repurposed. Early Marrow Broadcast was deliberately inaudible to anyone without the right implants, functioning as a covert communication channel as much as an art form. That tradition of deliberate imperceptibility persists in the contemporary genre's culture: sharing a Marrow Broadcast track is considered an intimate act, and public performance is structurally impossible, making every listening experience inherently personal and every act of distribution a gesture of trust.
creator: various
tier_availability: Originated in Lower tiers; now practiced across all tiers; distribution exclusively through direct implant-to-implant transfer or encrypted subdermal-compatible file sharing; no broadcast or streaming infrastructure exists by deliberate community choice
legality: Legal; subdermal transmission hardware exists in a regulatory gray zone in several districts; some compositions have been flagged as potential covert communication tools by security agencies
audience: Individuals with bone-conduction or subdermal implants across all tiers; intimacy-seeking communities; people who value music as private rather than social experience; security-conscious individuals who appreciate the genre's inherent undetectability
cultural_impact: Marrow Broadcast has developed one of the most distinctive and tightly-knit fan communities in GLMZ, defined by the intimacy of its distribution model — in a city saturated with broadcast media and neural feeds accessible to anyone, music that can only be shared person-to-person carries a weight of exclusivity and trust that upper-tier luxury markets have tried and failed to replicate. The genre has also had unintended political consequences: its infrastructure of encrypted subdermal file-sharing has been repurposed by activist and resistance communities as a communication network, a use that security agencies are aware of but find structurally difficult to address without criminalizing the genre outright.
story_hooks: A character receives a Marrow Broadcast track through what should have been a secure personal transfer, but the track contains a secondary signal beneath the music — a message, or possibly a passive surveillance tool — and tracing the chain of sharing backward means navigating a web of intimate trust relationships nobody wants disturbed.

A legendary Marrow Broadcast composer has gone silent for three years; her last track, circulating in increasingly degraded copies through the subdermal sharing network, is rumored to contain something in its lower frequencies that no one who has listened all the way through can agree on.

A security contractor is tasked with infiltrating a resistance cell that uses Marrow Broadcast infrastructure for communications — which means getting close enough to the right people to receive tracks directly, in a community where that kind of proximity means something real.
